protocol: 8 epochs x 1000 steps, dt 0.5 ms, 5-synapse graph, VYBFLY_MAX_ACTIVE = n (uncapped), stimulus = sparse_prop's built-in mt19937_64(1337) schedule for that n (scripts/make_stim.cpp reproduces the published s1/s80 files byte-for-byte)

graph_builder.what: reads the canonical 1x out-CSR, applies the 5-synapse rule, and writes the c-times CSR in Vyb (no Python in the graph path)
graph_builder.validation: at factor 1 the three output files are md5-identical to the published s1 CSR (indptr e8e3c7906bc9a3240b0968e279966158, indices 22ac60e4d80635eeede8580f5718f8df, syn b71c97ae704d777d5e3e0fa5fb8feef0)
graph_builder.policy_note: target child within the partner family is (edge + 7919*k) mod c; sibling edges omitted (see the header of the program)

runs.zero_copy_note: the two ranks ran different Vyb checkouts (lefty vyb-k, righty ursela-fly/vyb), so rank 1 took the copy path (dtoh_ms 13.9 s); the digests are unaffected
runs.rtx3090_note: 4.62x the one-GB10 time at that scale; 3,831,400 of 270,051,300 edges escape the u8 weight code to f32

oracle_100x.note: the CPU engine's max_active was hardcoded to 300000, which overflowed 1.6e9 spikes at 100x; it now reads VYBFLY_MAX_ACTIVE like the GPU engines do

hosts.two_spark: lefty (192.168.192.1) + righty (192.168.192.2), DGX Spark GB10, direct 200 GbE, RoCE v2
